window.part_of_day: afternoon (after the move forward; the hour is not stated)
window.note: the regiment was ordered forward again "after remaining here a short time"; the report does not say the works were finished

quote: July 1, marched to near Gettysburg, and, after moving forward to near the brick seminary, we were ordered to throw up breastworks.
notes: ordered to throw up breastworks; method, material and completion not stated, so the clip is a stand-in. Seed row of the plan: second reading owed by us-1c.

window.note: the colonel found it in the afternoon fight; he supposes it was made earlier that day

place.text: the foot of Seminary Ridge, about 40 yards in front of the battery

quote: Down the slope, some 40 yards in front of this battery, I found a slight breastwork of loose rails, which, I suppose, had been thrown together by some of our troops in the earlier part of the day, behind which I threw the regiment.
tier_basis: the colonel of the 7th Wisconsin found the rails piled and only supposes ("I suppose") that Union troops had thrown them together earlier that day: the pile is stated, the builder and the hour are his supposition
context_quote: in the engagement at Gettysburg on July 1: We left our camp, on the road running from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg
notes: Identified with E-01 of structures/works_stages.json by place (the foot of Seminary Ridge, in front of a battery) and day: the colonel does not name it. The row documents the pile and who used it (the 7th Wisconsin, us-1c-1d-meredith-7wi), not who built it. Seed row: second reading owed by us-1c.
